summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for evaluation of recurrent chest pain occurring at rest and after dialysis. Initial workup revealed nonspecific EKG changes and a stable, baseline-elevated troponin. A dipyridamole nuclear stress test showed a new reversible perfusion defect in the inferior wall, suggesting restenosis of a prior coronary stent. The patient underwent cardiac catheterization, which confirmed in-stent restenosis in the right coronary artery, and successfully received a new drug-eluting stent. He remained stable post-procedure, completed a scheduled hemodialysis session, and was discharged home in good condition. Medication changes included switching from atenolol to Toprol XL, adding lisinopril, and adjusting simvastatin and cinacalcet doses. Follow-up was arranged with a new cardiologist.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
